title: Paranormal Activity: A shocking live horror production at The Lowry
excerpt: You may have watched the Paranormal Activity films in the comfort of your own home, but did you know you […]
content:
You may have watched the Paranormal Activity films in the comfort of your own home, but did you know you could experience it in real life too?

You cannot choose to keep the light on in this stage play directed by Felix Barrett and written by thriller playwright Levi Holloway. Paranormal Activity is a stand alone story set in the same universe as the iconic movie series.

The story follows newly wed couple, James and Lou, after they move to London from Chicago. Despite aiming for a fresh start, they quickly learn that paranormal activity seems to haunt them wherever they go. 

As a horror fanatic I will admit I walked into this experience far too smug, curious to see how a play could possibly emulate the same fear and horror tactics as the movies. I can now attest that I was severely humbled.

The first thought I had after leaving the theatre was simply that this was horror done right. A truly gripping and dark story that sticks with you after the lights come on and horror taken seriously in a true piece of theatrical brilliance.

Levi Holloway,  the Writer said that: “Good horror feels like it’s talking just to you, cutting like a knife through all the noise, whispering something you’ve always known but have forgotten or have tried a thousand times over to mute. Something once you hear, you can’t stop listening to.

“Good horror doesn’t rob you of sleep, it rules it.”

I have never wanted a play to finish so soon whilst at the same time singing its praises so highly.

The attention to detail in the lighting by Anna Watson was impeccable. The constant range of bright lights to darkness had me wishing I could just turn my phone torch on to check there was nothing hiding under my seat. 

This was matched perfectly with the set and costume design by Fly Davis. We were welcomed in to a warm and homely environment, only to rip that away and shock everyone with chill and discomfort.

The jump scares were perfectly unpredictable and growingly shocking as the play went on. The illusions by Chris Fisher still have me wondering ‘how on earth did they pull that off?’.

I have to give special praise for the sound design by Gareth Fry. The subtle drone sounds throughout as well as the ear-splitting noises heightened the tension of the play entirely, it wouldn’t have been nearly such a scare fest without it.

Thanks to the flawless production in in this play, they really hit the nail on the head in the world of horror. If you are a fan of the film series, I am sure you will not be disappointed.

Lead actors James Bye and Hannah Sinclair Robinson bounced naturally off each other, giving a sincere performance that captured the ‘found footage’ energy of Paranormal Activity.

The play first opened at London’s Ambassadors Theatre in December last year and it’s scheduled to continue being performed in the West End until February 27 2027.

For any horror fans I can’t stress enough how much of an unmissable experience this is. However, for any scaredy-cats, be sure to hold onto your drink tight, you will never quite predict the moment you will be jumping out of your seat.
